questions.question: What is different about castor seeds?

options.text: It is the only rabi crop
It is neither rabi nor kharif
It is both rabi and kharif crop

questions.solution:
The correct answer is It is __**both rabi and kharif crop.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__ **

__
 
• ** Castor seeds are a unique crop as they can be grown in both rabi and kharif seasons.**
 
• This means that farmers have the flexibility to cultivate** castor seeds twice a year.**
 
• Castor seeds are also known as non-food oilseed crops.
 
• They are primarily grown for their oil, which is used in a variety of industries such as pharmaceuticals, cosmetics, and lubricants.
 
• Castor seeds require **warm temperatures and well-drained soil to grow.**
 
• They are not suitable for areas with **heavy rainfall or high humidity.**
 
• Castor seeds are also known for their high resistance to pests and diseases. This makes them a low-maintenance crop, which is ideal for small farmers who may not have access to expensive pesticides.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Rabi crops are those that are sown in the winter and harvested in the spring. Examples of rabi crops include wheat, barley, and mustard.
 
• Kharif crops are those that are sown in the rainy season and harvested in the autumn. Examples of Kharif crops include rice, maize, and cotton.
 
• Zaid crops are those that are grown in the summer season between rabi and kharif. Examples of zaid crops include watermelon, cucumber, and bitter gourd.

**Therefore, the cost of production of the article is Rs. 600.**

questions.question: A can complete 3/4th of the work in 9 days and B can complete 2/5th of the work in 12 days. With the help of C, all three together complete the whole work in 60/11 days and earn Rs. 330. If money is shared in the ratio of work done, then find the difference in the share of C and the share of A (approximately).
questions.solution:
**Given:**

A's time = 9 days for 3/4th work,

B's time = 12 days for 2/5th work,

A + B + C's time = 60/11 days,

Total earnings = Rs. 330

**Concept:**

Shares of A, B, C are proportional to the amount of work they did in the given time

**Calculation:**

Calculate the total shares of A, B, and C.

Time taken by A to complete the whole work = 9 × 4/3 = 12 days

Time taken by B to complete the whole work = 12 × 5/2 = 30 days

Time taken by all three = 60/11 days

LCM of 12, 30, and 60/11 = 60

So, Let the total work be 60 units

Efficiency of A = 60/12 = 5

Efficiency of B = 60/30 = 2

Efficiency of all three = 60/(60/11) = 11

Efficiency of C = Eff.(A+B+C) - Eff.(A + B)

⇒ Efficiency of C = 11 - (5+2)

⇒ 11 - 7 = 4

Thus, Efficiency of C = 4 units

Now, the amount of work done by A in 60/11 days ⇒ 5 × 60/11 = 300/11

The amount of work done by B in 60/11 days ⇒ 2 × 60/11 = 120/11

The amount of work done by C in 60/11 days ⇒ 4 × 60/11 = 240/11

Ratio of work done of A, B, and C =300/11 : 120/11 : 240/11 = 5 : 2 : 4

Since, Total shares = Sum of the ratio of work done,

So, Sum of ratio of work done = 5 + 2 + 4 = 11 units

⇒ Total shares = 11 units

⇒ 330 = 11 units

⇒ 1 unit = 30

⇒ A's share = 30 × 5 = Rs. 150

⇒ C's share = 30 × 4 = Rs. 120

The difference in the share of A and C = 150 - 120 

⇒ Rs. 30

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 30**
